players.product: Applied HVAC for data centers: medium- and large-capacity chillers, custom air handling units and air-side equipment (Daikin Applied)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Koichi Takahashi: in Q1 both net sales and operating profit reached record highs and operating profit exceeded the company's internal target, including the weak-yen conversion effect and refunds from U.S. tariffs; the operating profit margin decreased by 0.8 percentage points YoY because cost increases (Middle East crisis, emerging-market currency depreciation, additional U.S. tariffs, soaring raw material prices) exceeded initial projections. He assesses Q1 progress as generally in line with plan, with this year's cost-reduction effects materializing in earnest from Q2; the annual plan was not revised because Q2 is the air-conditioning peak season, and the company aims first to deliver the annual plan.
quarterly_data.figure: record-high Q1 net sales and operating profit; operating profit margin down 0.8 percentage points YoY

quarterly_data.signal: North America residential (Daikin Comfort Technologies North America, DNA): Q1 sales 112% of the prior year on a yen basis and 102% in local currency; market share approximately 23% for the three months, up about 3 percentage points YoY. IR head Yuri Sakamoto: volume contributed a positive 10 points, pricing strategy a positive 2 points, product mix and other factors a negative 10 points, with no M&A effect. CFO: demand limited by inflation, high mortgage rates and Middle East uncertainty, and more customers seek lower-priced products; the eco-premium Fit line started slowly in April-May but reached 112% of the prior year in June and approximately 150% in July. Q1 operating profit margin was 11% at DNA North America and 9% at DAA North America; the North America air-conditioning operating margin declined 2 percentage points YoY, in line with expectations.
quarterly_data.figure: DNA sales 112% (yen) / 102% (local currency); share approximately 23%; DNA North America operating margin 11%, DAA North America 9%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the North American channel and pricing: Daikin's wholesale inventory is roughly on par with last year, so the adjustment of distribution inventory has largely completed; actual retail sales have been significantly higher than the prior year since around February, though growth is not particularly strong. The company's basic policy is to steadily raise prices (it prioritizes price over volume, using simulation data by region); for Fit it is adding compact and easy-to-install models, supporting dealers until they sell 10 units, and offering financing including leases.

Cost headwinds: IR head Yuri Sakamoto said the Q1 profit bridge includes a direct negative impact of JPY4.6 billion from U.S. tariffs and a positive effect of JPY10.5 billion from tariff refunds. CFO: additional tariffs on iron, copper and aluminum and on imports from Mexico raised costs more than anticipated; copper has by far the greatest raw-material impact and the company, which hedges copper mainly domestically, could not hedge even half of the total; naphtha-derived materials and trucking rates also weigh. Price increases have been decided by product line and region, with pricing measures in May and August (some moved up by about a month; the CFO says they are decided rather than implemented, as some phases start in August); management expects the cost issue to be resolved by the end of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. tariffs -JPY4.6 billion; tariff refunds +JPY10.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: with inventory being reduced as planned, production capacity utilization rose to the low 70s in Q1 from the high 60s a year earlier, and inventory turnover is already more efficient than originally planned; utilization should increase further if inventory reduction and sales volumes follow plan, with a decision after reviewing Q2 results.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity utilization in the low 70s (high 60s a year earlier)

quarterly_data.signal: Chemicals, CFO: the semiconductor sector is performing exceptionally well - fluoropolymers for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, fluoropolymers used in production and fine chemicals; PFA, primarily used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, is highly profitable, and FEP fluoropolymer used in data-center cables is also performing very well. After two years of distribution-inventory adjustment the trend has reversed: actual demand has grown significantly and is expected to keep rising, customers who insisted on not increasing inventory now want to carry a certain amount, and demand for building distribution inventory is very strong. The fluorochemicals business contributed above expectations in Q1; management has high hopes for Q2 and beyond.

Europe: the heat wave boosted sales in parts of May and June (notably France) and shipment volumes are very strong, but price pressure from Chinese manufacturers, who are shifting to exports toward Europe, Asia and Latin America, is extremely intense. CFO: Daikin will not compete in the volume segment, focusing on multi-split and system products and on commercial (hotels, now also schools and hospitals) and applied business; the fiscal-year operating margin target for Europe is unchanged at 4% to 5% and progress is on schedule; some applied shipments were halted due to the Middle East situation. IR head: Europe Q1 sales were 108% of the prior year in local currency.
quarterly_data.figure: Europe margin target 4% to 5%; Q1 sales 108% in local currency

quarterly_data.signal: China and Asia: China residential multi-split air-conditioner sales fell to 86% of the prior year amid the real estate slump, but the CFO says Daikin outperformed market growth and kept high profit margins (no industry statistics; he believes growth exceeded the industry's). India air-conditioning revenue grew to 128% of the prior year in local currency (low prior-year base due to weather); in ASEAN consumer spending fell and large construction projects were delayed, and Asia profitability declined partly on emerging-market currency depreciation. From Q2 the company will expand mid- to high-end residential models and products for data centers, where demand remains strong.
quarterly_data.figure: China residential multi-split 86% YoY; India 128% YoY (local currency)

quarterly_data.signal: FUSION30 progress, CFO: to minimize U.S. tariffs SKY production is being transferred from Thailand to the United States; to meet strong data-center cooling demand while keeping investment in check the company is establishing a production system using leased factories; more than a dozen low-profitability businesses have operating-margin targets and restructuring plans, and in Q1 they improved YoY but were slightly behind target, with the filter business and the European refrigeration business slightly delayed. The share of the solutions business in air-conditioning revenue will be disclosed from the Q2 earnings report.
